Cover — How to read

Design Patterns
Creational · Structural · Behavioral
Modules built for another developer’s client code
Purpose
Patterns are shared answers to recurring design pressures. They help you shape module boundaries so callers get a calm, intention-revealing API while the module stays free to grow, swap internals, or add variants without rewriting every consumer.
Developer experience goal
Treat each slide as a handover story: you own the module; another developer owns the client. Good patterns make that handover kind—small surface area, clear abstractions, and room to extend the module graciously so clients keep writing the same simple calls.
How to read each pattern slide
Problem / Solution
Why the current shape hurts, and what the pattern changes about dependencies and responsibilities.
Before / After UML
Always includes a Client box. Follow dashed arrows from Client to see what caller code must know. After should depend on a narrow API, not a pile of concretes.
Client Code
How the other developer uses (or is forced to misuse) your module.
Module Code
The API boundary you hand over—the implementation clients should not need to reopen when requirements grow.
Look for fewer Client dependencies after the pattern, and for module code that stays easy to use while remaining easy to extend.

Singleton

Singleton
Creational Design Pattern
Ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.
CASE STUDY: Shared Config across services
01 / 14
Problem
• User drives UserService / OrderService / ReportService; each needs Config. • Call order is not fixed—any service may run first. • Each service copies if config == null: config = new Config() → multiple instances.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
• User still calls doWork(); services only call Config.getInstance(). • The null-check and construction live once inside Config. • First caller creates it; every service shares that instance.
After (using Singleton)
Service Code (Before)
Pseudocode
// inside each service (User API unchanged)
if config == null:
config = new Config()
config.load()
// same guard in UserService, OrderService, ReportService
Service Code (After)
Pseudocode
// inside each service (User API unchanged)
config = Config.getInstance()
config.load()
// same load; guard moved into Config
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — Config singleton (owns the lazy init)
private static instance
private Config(): load()
static getInstance():
if instance == null:
instance = new Config()
return instance
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/singleton
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Factory Method

Factory Method
Creational Design Pattern
Provides an interface for creating objects, but lets subclasses decide which class to instantiate.
CASE STUDY: Plane, truck, and ship transport
02 / 14
Problem
• Client code needs to create different types of objects (e.g. Plane, Truck, Ship). • The client contains conditional logic and knows about all concrete classes. • Adding a new type requires modifying client code (violates Open/Closed Principle). • Object creation logic is scattered and duplicated across the application. • Client is tightly coupled to concrete classes.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
• Define a factory interface/class for creating products (e.g. Transport). • Concrete factory decides which concrete product to instantiate. • Client code works with the factory and the product interface, not concrete classes. • To add a new type, add a new product and update the factory (client code unchanged). • Centralizes and encapsulates object creation logic.
After (using Factory Method)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
plane = new Plane(); plane.fly()
truck = new Truck(); truck.drive()
ship = new Ship(); ship.sail()
// three types; three different method names
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
fleet = [factory.create("plane"),
factory.create("truck"),
factory.create("ship")]
for t in fleet: t.transport()
// same three results; one Transport method
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — creation API for client developers
// TransportFactory.create(type)
if type == "plane": return new Plane()
elif type == "truck": return new Truck()
elif type == "ship": return new Ship()
// Plane/Truck/Ship implement Transport.transport()
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/factory-method
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Abstract Factory

Abstract Factory
Creational Design Pattern
Create related product families through a factory interface.
CASE STUDY: UPS and DHL transport families
03 / 14
Problem
Client news every carrier concrete and calls drive / sail / fly separately.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Pick a family factory; create as Transport; one transport() loop.
After (using Abstract Factory)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
dt = new DHLTruck(); dt.drive()
ds = new DHLShip(); ds.sail()
dp = new DHLPlane(); dp.fly()
ut = new UPSTruck(); ut.drive()
us = new UPSShip(); us.sail()
up = new UPSPlane(); up.fly()
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
dhl = new DHLFactory()
dp = dhl.createPlane(); ds = dhl.createShip(); dt = dhl.createTruck()
ups = new UPSFactory()
up = ups.createPlane(); us = ups.createShip(); ut = ups.createTruck()
fleet = [dp, ds, dt, up, us, ut]
for t in fleet: t.transport()
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/abstract-factory
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Builder

Builder
Creational Design Pattern
Separate construction steps from the representation being assembled.
CASE STUDY: Houses with optional features
04 / 14
Problem
• House grows telescoping constructors (rooms/doors/windows + pool/trees/…). • Client passes long positional bool lists—unclear which flag is which. • Adding a feature forces new overloads and updates every call site.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
• HouseBuilder names each step; ConcreteHouseBuilder adds extras. • HouseDirector encodes recipes (simple / family); Client can also chain steps. • Same houses; readable construction; product is House.
After (using Builder)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
houseA = new House(1, 1, 1)
houseB = new House(2, 2, 1, false, false, true, true)
houseC = new House(4, 3, 3, true, false, false, true)
houseD = new House(2, 1, 2, false, true, false, false)
houseE = new House(6, 4, 5, true, true, true, true)
// five houses; magic bool positions
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
director = new HouseDirector()
houseA = director.buildSimpleHouse(new ConcreteHouseBuilder())
houseB = new ConcreteHouseBuilder().addWindow().addWindow()
.addDoor().addDoor().addRoom().addStatues().addGarden().getResult()
houseC = director.buildFamilyHouse(new ConcreteHouseBuilder())
houseD = new ConcreteHouseBuilder().addWindow().addWindow()
.addDoor().addRoom().addRoom().addTrees().getResult()
houseE = new ConcreteHouseBuilder()
.addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow().addWindow()
.addDoor().addDoor().addDoor().addDoor()
.addRoom().addRoom().addRoom().addRoom().addRoom()
.addPool().addTrees().addStatues().addGarden().getResult()
// same five houses; named steps / director recipes
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/builder
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Adapter

Adapter
Structural Design Pattern
Translate an existing interface into the interface a client expects.
CASE STUDY: XML stock data and JSON analytics
05 / 14
Problem
The stock app supplies XML; the analytics library requires JSON.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Adapter inherits AnalyticsService and composes JsonAnalyticsLibrary; converts then delegates.
After (using Adapter)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
xml = provider.getStockData()
json = convertXmlToJson(xml)
report = library.analyze(json)
// same stock report; client does the conversion
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
xml = provider.getStockData()
report = adapter.analyze(xml)
// same stock report; adapter owns the conversion
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — AnalyticsService API for client developers
// XmlAnalyticsAdapter extends AnalyticsService
// composes library: JsonAnalyticsLibrary
// analyze(xml):
// json = convert(xml)
// return library.analyze(json)
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/adapter
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Bridge

Bridge
Structural Design Pattern
Separate two independent dimensions so both can evolve independently.
CASE STUDY: Shapes and colors
06 / 14
Problem
Each shape/color combination requires another subclass.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Shapes hold a Color reference instead of encoding color in inheritance.
After (using Bridge)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
new RedCircle().draw()
new BlueSquare().draw()
// red circle + blue square; one class per combo
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
shapes = [new Circle(new Red()),
new Square(new Blue())]
for s in shapes: s.draw()
// same two drawings; compose shape × color
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — Shape API for client developers
// Circle.draw()
color.apply()
renderCircleGeometry()
// color and geometry vary independently
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/bridge
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Facade

Facade
Structural Design Pattern
Expose a simple entry point to a complex subsystem.
CASE STUDY: Video conversion subsystem
07 / 14
Problem
Every client coordinates codecs, bitrate conversion, and audio repair.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
A facade orchestrates the subsystem behind one conversion call.
After (using Facade)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
codec = CodecFactory.extract(file)
raw = BitrateReader.read(file, codec)
video = BitrateReader.convert(raw, mp4)
result = AudioMixer.fix(video)
// export file as mp4 via subsystem steps
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
result = new VideoConverter().convert(file, "mp4")
// same mp4 export; one facade call
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — VideoConverter facade API for client developers
// VideoConverter.convert(file, format)
source = CodecFactory.extract(file)
raw = BitrateReader.read(file, source)
video = BitrateReader.convert(raw, codecFor(format))
return AudioMixer.fix(video)
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/facade
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Proxy

Proxy
Structural Design Pattern
A stand-in object that controls access to a real service without changing its interface.
CASE STUDY: Expensive database service with caching
08 / 14
Problem
• The real service is expensive to create or use (e.g. database, remote API, large object). • Repeated queries can be slow and waste resources. • The client may need to handle initialization or access control logic. • We want extra behavior (caching, logging, access control) without changing client code.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
• Introduce a proxy that implements the same interface as the real service. • The proxy controls access, adding lazy init, caching, logging, or access control. • Client uses the same interface—only the class it instantiates changes. • Adds: caching, lazy initialization, optional access control and logging.
After (using Proxy)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
db = new ExpensiveDatabaseService()
r1 = db.query("users")
r2 = db.query("users")
// two "users" results; two expensive hits
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
db = new DatabaseProxy()
r1 = db.query("users")
r2 = db.query("users")
// same two "users" results; second from cache
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — DatabaseService API for client developers
// DatabaseProxy.query(key)
if cache.contains(key): return cache[key]
if realService == null: realService = new RealDatabaseService()
result = realService.query(key)
cache[key] = result; return result
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/proxy
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Composite

Composite
Structural Design Pattern
Treat individual objects and recursive groups through one interface.
CASE STUDY: Boxes containing products and boxes
09 / 14
Problem
Pricing code distinguishes products from nested boxes repeatedly.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
A box sums child prices; each child follows the same contract.
After (using Composite)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
total = 0
for item in order.contents:
if item is Product: total += item.price
else: total += priceNestedBox(item)
// price of product + nested box
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
total = order.getPrice()
// same total; one getPrice() on OrderItem
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — OrderItem API for client developers
// Box.getPrice()
total = 0
for child in children:
total += child.getPrice()
return total
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/composite
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Template Method

Template Method
Behavioral Design Pattern
Fix an algorithm’s order while subclasses implement selected steps.
CASE STUDY: Mining PDF and CSV documents
10 / 14
Problem
Format-specific miners duplicate the processing and reporting pipeline.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Move the sequence into a base method; override extraction only.
After (using Template Method)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
pdfReport = analyze(pdf.extract(pdfPath))
csvReport = analyze(csv.extract(csvPath))
// two reports; client repeats extract+analyze
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
miners = [new PdfMiner(), new CsvMiner()]
reports = []
for m in miners: reports.add(m.mine(pathFor(m)))
// same two reports; one mine() pipeline each
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — DataMiner.mine API for client developers
// DataMiner.mine(path): fixed sequence
data = extract(path)
return analyze(data)
// PdfMiner.extract(path): return parsePdf(path)
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/template-method
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Strategy

Strategy
Behavioral Design Pattern
Make alternative algorithms interchangeable through a shared contract.
CASE STUDY: Navigation route algorithms
11 / 14
Problem
A navigator grows conditionals for road, walking, and transit routes.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Delegate routing to a strategy selected by the client.
After (using Strategy)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
road = roadRoute(a, b)
walk = walkRoute(a, b)
transit = transitRoute(a, b)
// three routes; client branches per mode
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
for s in [new RoadRoute(), new WalkingRoute(),
new TransitRoute()]:
navigator.setStrategy(s)
routes.add(navigator.buildRoute(a, b))
// same three routes; one buildRoute() API
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — Navigator API for client developers
// Navigator.buildRoute(a, b)
return strategy.buildRoute(a, b)
// WalkingRoute builds pedestrian paths
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/strategy
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

State

State
Behavioral Design Pattern
Delegate behavior to an object representing the current state.
CASE STUDY: Document publication workflow
12 / 14
Problem
Publication rules accumulate in a switch over document status.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Each state handles publish and can transition the document.
After (using State)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
doc.status = "draft"
doc.status = "moderation" // submit
doc.status = "published" // admin approve
// draft → moderation → published via status ifs
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
doc = new Document(new Draft())
doc.publish(user) // enters moderation
doc.publish(admin) // becomes published
// same draft → moderation → published path
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — Document.publish API for client developers
// Moderation.publish(doc, user)
if user.isAdmin:
doc.changeState(new Published())
// Published.publish(...) does nothing
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/state
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Observer

Observer
Behavioral Design Pattern
Notify registered subscribers when a publisher emits an event.
CASE STUDY: Editor events notify logging and email
13 / 14
Problem
Editor logic directly invokes concrete logging and email services.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Publish an event; subscribers handle their own reactions.
After (using Observer)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
editor.saveFile()
logger.write(file.name)
mailer.send(file.name)
// save + log + email; client wires reactions
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
events.subscribe("save", new LogListener())
events.subscribe("save", new EmailListener())
editor.saveFile()
// same save + log + email; listeners react
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — EventManager API for client developers
// EventManager.notify(type, data)
for listener in listeners[type]:
listener.update(data)
// Editor.saveFile(): write(); events.notify("save", name)
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/observer
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency

Command

Command
Behavioral Design Pattern
Represent a request as an object that can be invoked and undone.
CASE STUDY: Undoable text-editor actions
14 / 14
Problem
Buttons and shortcuts duplicate editing actions without shared undo.
Before (direct coupling)
Solution
Bind both triggers to a command; store successful edits in history.
After (using Command)
Client Code (Before)
Pseudocode
pasteButton.click() // editor.insert(text)
shortcut.press() // editor.insert(text)
// paste from two triggers; logic duplicated, no undo
Client Code (After)
Pseudocode
paste = new PasteCommand(editor, text)
pasteButton.bind(() => app.execute(paste))
shortcut.bind(() => app.execute(paste))
pasteButton.click(); shortcut.press()
// same two pastes via shared command
Module Code (API boundary)
Pseudocode
// MODULE — Command API for client developers
// PasteCommand.execute()
backup = editor.text; editor.insert(text)
return true // app records command in history
// undo(): editor.text = backup
Source: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/command
UML: Client box = caller code; hollow triangle = inheritance / realization; dashed open arrow = dependency
